topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture on the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate immune recognition: PAMPs, DAMPs, and self-discrimination
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the principles by which the innate immune system identifies infections and tissue injury through microbial and damage-associated molecular patterns.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptors and intracellular signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic encoding, subcellular distribution, and signaling cascades of pattern recognition receptors, including Toll-like receptors, cytosolic sensors, and the inflammasome.

topics.label: Cellular mediators, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how sentinel cells initiate inflammatory signaling, recruit circulating leukocytes into damaged tissues, facilitate lymphatic antigen drainage, and can cause systemic pathology such as septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the active and passive mechanisms that terminate inflammation, the tissue healing process, and the adaptations or pathologies that arise when resolution fails.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic marks the conclusion of the lecture and previews the upcoming topic.
